text: A pressure change applied to a confined fluid is transmitted throughout it. A hydraulic system uses this to connect forces at separated pistons.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.3; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-3-pascals-principle-and-hydraulics. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: In an ideal hydraulic lift with pistons at the same height, a larger output piston produces more force at the same pressure. It travels a shorter distance than the smaller input piston.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.3; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-3-pascals-principle-and-hydraulics. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: A hydraulic lift multiplies force without multiplying work: the smaller piston must move farther to displace the volume needed by the larger piston.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.3; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-3-pascals-principle-and-hydraulics. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: For steady incompressible flow through a tube, volume flow rate stays constant. A narrower cross-section therefore requires a higher average speed.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.5; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-5-fluid-dynamics. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: A streamline follows the local direction of fluid velocity. In steady flow, the velocity pattern at each fixed position does not change with time.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.5; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-5-fluid-dynamics. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: For steady, incompressible flow with negligible friction, Bernoulli's equation balances pressure, kinetic energy per volume, and gravitational energy per volume along a streamline.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.6; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-6-bernoullis-equation. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: An ideal flow speeds up in a narrowed tube and has lower static pressure there when elevation is unchanged. A constriction can therefore create a measurable pressure difference.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.6; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-6-bernoullis-equation. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: A fast jet can create a low-pressure region that draws another fluid into the stream. An atomizer uses moving air to pick up droplets of liquid.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.6; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-6-bernoullis-equation. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: Viscosity resists neighboring layers of fluid sliding past one another. In a tube, the walls slow the adjacent fluid.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.7; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-7-viscosity-and-turbulence. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: For steady laminar flow of a Newtonian fluid in a circular tube, Poiseuille's law makes flow rate proportional to the fourth power of radius. A small constriction can have a large effect.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.7; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-7-viscosity-and-turbulence. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: Under Poiseuille's assumptions, doubling a tube's length halves its flow rate if its radius, fluid viscosity, and pressure difference stay fixed.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.7; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-7-viscosity-and-turbulence. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: Reynolds number compares inertial and viscous effects. It helps assess whether a flow is likely to remain orderly or become turbulent.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 14.7; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-7-viscosity-and-turbulence. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: A wetting liquid can rise inside a narrow tube as adhesive and cohesive effects shape its meniscus. For otherwise equal conditions, a narrower tube produces a larger rise.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, section 11.8; https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/11-8-cohesion-and-adhesion-in-liquids-surface-tension-and-capillary-action. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: The contact angle shows how a liquid meets a solid surface. The balance between adhesion and cohesion can make a drop spread out or bead up.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, section 11.8; https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/11-8-cohesion-and-adhesion-in-liquids-surface-tension-and-capillary-action. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: Surface tension tends to reduce a liquid's exposed area. A small object can be supported by the deformed surface even when its material is denser than the liquid.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, section 11.8; https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/11-8-cohesion-and-adhesion-in-liquids-surface-tension-and-capillary-action. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: A primed siphon can move water over a high point to an outlet below the source reservoir. The difference in water levels supplies the gravitational drive.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Hughes and Gurung, Exploring the boundary between a siphon and barometer in a hypobaric chamber, Scientific Reports 4, 4741 (2014); https://www.nature.com/articles/srep04741. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Pressure near the top of an ordinary siphon is below ambient pressure. Lowering the ambient pressure can make the water boil at the crest and interrupt continuous flow.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Hughes and Gurung, Exploring the boundary between a siphon and barometer in a hypobaric chamber, Scientific Reports 4, 4741 (2014); https://www.nature.com/articles/srep04741. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Special experiments with prepared water have operated siphons above the usual barometric height limit. A liquid can sustain tension, but bubbles and cavitation often limit ordinary setups.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Boatwright, Hughes and Barry, The height limit of a siphon, Scientific Reports 5, 16790 (2015); https://www.nature.com/articles/srep16790. Consulted 2026-10-13.
